newsitem.title: USA: White House says cannot stop Carville attack on Starr.
newsitem.headline: White House says cannot stop Carville attack on Starr.

text.p: The White House said Monday political adviser James Carville's attacks on independent counsel Kenneth Starr did not reflect President Clinton's thinking but doubted the criticism could be stopped.

"Mr. Carville is certainly someone who speaks for himself and has made it clear he will speak for himself, regardless of what the White House says," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters in his daily briefing.

"It does not represent the president's thinking," McCurry added. "The president, on this matter, will speak for himself or instruct those of us who speak on his behalf to indicate whatever he wants said. And he's indicated that the work of the independent counsel ought to be treated respectfully and with the proper no comment."

Carville, a key adviser in Clinton's 1992 election, has repeatedly attacked Starr, who is investigating the Whitewater land deal in Arkansas in which Clinton and his wife Hillary invested more than a decade ago.
Starr's inquiry has expanded to including the firing of the White House travel office staff in 1993 and the White House's improperly obtaining confidential FBI files on top Republicans.
Last month, Carville said he was setting up a group to attack Starr, suggesting that the lawyer, a Republican, was using his power "to advance the right-wing agenda."

McCurry said Clinton and Carville had not discussed the matter and he danced around the question of whether other White House officials had raised the topic, saying he was not aware of any "extensive discussion" with Carville.

Asked why the president himself did not stop Carville from criticising Starr, McCurry replied: "He's not in a position to dissuade Mr. Carville from pursuing the course that Mr. Carville (has chosen)."
